newsitem.title: UK: London gold corrects ahead of option expiry.
newsitem.headline: London gold corrects ahead of option expiry.

text.p: Precious metals markets led by gold and silver began to correct on Tuesday afternoon having moved sharply higher in New York on Monday.
"A gain of $4.00 in some 20 minutes last night might have been a bit ambitious. We are coming down to a more commonsense level now," one dealer said.
Gold fixed at $353.70 per ounce after $357.25 in the morning and a Monday afternoon fixing of $353.60.
Silver also trimmed its gains of the past five days to be indicated at $4.96/$4.98 after hitting a stumbling block of resistance around $5.07.
"Given the OTC option expiry tomorrow afternoon, $5.00 seems comfortable for silver for the time being," a dealer said.

Silver broke above $5.00 late on Monday as part of a 30-cent rally spread over the previous four days for the first time since last October and fixed this morning at $5.03, its highest fixing since October 14, 1996.
Dealers said silver had done good business on the way up and had given an opportunity to take profits for buyers at over $5.00.
"They can come in again at $4.97 or thereabouts and we could set up nice bit of range trading here," a dealer said.
For gold though, the auguries seemed to suggest a move lower rather than higher ahead of Wednesday's option expiry.
Dealers said there was a gap on the February Comex chart around around $352.50-$353.30 which could become the target for gold on the downside before the next upswing.

"Gold is not in a bull market yet, but we have already done $10 in the past week. I'ld expect to see a correction before it goes further," a dealer said, adding that today's slippage had done "no overall damage".
Gold could edge lower before the option expiry which had been concentrated on the $350 strikes. "I think we'll see it around there by the expiry, rather than try for $360," the dealer said.
Platinum and palladium turned a little easier with the two principal markets.
It was indicated at $356.95/$357.95, down $2.80 from the Monday close and palladium was $1.50 lower at $121.50/$122.50.
